title: Precise cancel ACK probe and server-deadline negotiation for streaming lifecycle (OpenAI compat)
author: Marina Lopez
release_notes: Deterministic cancel ACK probing and server-client deadline negotiation for streaming requests. Less false-positive cancellations; safer function/tool call retry semantics; metrics and docs added.
description: Motivation: Customer signals from SUP-1278 and internal dogfooding showed spurious cancels when clients dropped mid-stream or when proxies inserted transient RSTs. Existing logic uses a best-effort cancel and optimistic resume which leads to two problems: (1) false-positive cancellation of in-flight tool/function calls and (2) inability to extend server-side deadlines when clients can tolerate a short reconnect window. This PR introduces a deterministic 'early-ACK probe' and a lightweight server-client deadline negotiation step that reduces both failure modes while preserving OpenAI-style compatibility. Design summary: 1) Early-ACK probe: when a client sends a cancel, the server responds with a short-lived ACK_PROBE token + probe_window (ms). The client must acknowledge receipt of the probe to confirm intent; lack of probe ACK within the window converts the cancel into a soft-cancel (keeps running to finish idempotent toolcalls). 2) Deadline negotiation: the server returns a negotiated_deadline (ISO8601 ms) when it believes finishing current toolcall is cheap; clients may defer hard-cancel until the negotiated_deadline. 3) Idempotent-tool semantics: add explicit nacks for non-idempotent tool calls when a confirmed cancel arrives, and make retry/backoff deterministic for idempotent tools. 4) Backwards compatibility: OpenAI-style clients that do not implement the probe simply see the previous behavior (cancel triggers best-effort stop) because probe fields are optional; we emit probe metadata only when the runtime detects in-flight non-trivial toolcalls. Checklist: - [x] Implement server-side ACK_PROBE/negotiated_deadline fields and serialization - [x] Add client-side probe ACK path in TS and Py SDKs - [x] Metrics: record probe latency, probe-missed rate, negotiated_deadline_utilization - [x] Unit and integration tests for confirmed vs. soft cancel transitions - [x] Docs: streaming cancel behavior and migration guide - [x] Manual QA: wrangler client reconnection scenarios Commits (high level): - initial: server/streaming: cancel negotiator and proto additions - client: sdk-ts/compat: probe ACK path and graceful fallback - client: sdk-py: streaming stream.py negotiation changes and tests - observability: add redwood.stream.cancel.probe_latency and redwood.stream.cancel.probe_missed_rate - docs: openai_compat/streaming-cancel.md with examples Changed areas (high level): - server/streaming/cancel_negotiator.go: core negotiation state machine (new) - server/streaming/cancel_negotiator_test.go: tests for confirm/soft-cancel flows - sdk/ts/openai_compat/probe_policy.ts: client probe ACK and fallback logic - sdk/python/redwood/stream.py: streaming client handles negotiated_deadline - docs/openai_compat/streaming-cancel.md: migration guide and examples - observability/metrics.yaml: new metrics and dashboard hints Example payloads (JSON embedded inline for reviewers): Server response when cancel accepted for probe: {"type":"cancel_ack","probe_window_ms":250,"probe_id":"p_8b2f","negotiated_deadline":"2026-02-22T14:03:12.123Z"} Client ACK (probe): {"type":"probe_ack","probe_id":"p_8b2f"} Small snippet from cancel_negotiator.go (illustrative): ``if cancelRequest.HasInFlightTool() && !tool.IsIdempotent() { emitNack(); return } startProbeWindow(probeWindowMs)`` Observability notes: added counters and histograms, tag by model/route and whether negotiation was offered. Operational knobs: runtime config keys added: streaming.cancel.probe_enabled (default true), streaming.cancel.probe_window_ms (default 300), streaming.cancel.max_negotiated_extension_ms (default 2000). Migration: default behavior is safe for all existing clients; customers can opt-out via runtime flag to restore old immediate-cancel behavior. Tests & QA: added unit tests covering timeouts, missed-probe fallback, and idempotency branch; ran integration with wrangler client against proxy-inserted RST and large toolcall workunits. Performance: small CPU overhead in runtime state machine (microbench shows +0.4% p99 CPU on e2e bench) and negligible latency for non-cancel paths. Security: no new secrets; probe IDs are ephemeral and logged at info-level only when debugging is enabled. Related: ENG-4892 (cancel reliability), ENG-4920 (toolcall idempotency), SUP-1278 (customer incident).

client-ts: implement probe ACK/fallback in openai_compat layer

docs: streaming-cancel migration guide and examples
review_comments: Evan Park (review): Can you clarify race between probe expiry and toolcall completion? Also add a metric for probe-missed -> soft-cancel transitions.
Marina Lopez (author): Added tests for toolcall race and a probe_missed_rate metric; clarified behavior in docs. Probe expiry favors soft-cancel unless tool is non-idempotent.
Priya Nair (review): Prefer shorter default probe_window (250ms) in high-throughput routes. Consider per-route override. Also requested a changelog blurb.
Marina Lopez (author): Made probe_window configurable per-route via runtime config; added release notes line and dashboard tile notes.
Jonas Schmidt (approve): Tests look solid, metrics in place, minor nits addressed. Approving for merge.
